answer_explanation: HCF=p²q³, so m+n=5; LCM=p³q⁴, so r+s=7. Hence (m+n)(r+s)=35.

answer_explanation: α+β=2/p and αβ=3. Equating gives 2/p=3, so p=2/3.

answer_explanation: For inconsistency, 3/(2k-1)=1/(k-1)≠1/(2k+1). Solving 3(k-1)=2k-1 gives k=2.

question_text: ABCD is a trapezium with AD ∥ BC and AD = 4cm. If the diagonals AC and BD intersect each other at O such that AO/OC = DO/OB =1/2, then BC =
answer_text: 8cm
answer_explanation: In a trapezium, AO/OC=AD/BC. Thus 1/2=4/BC, so BC=8 cm.

answer_text: 3√3cm

answer_text: 9π  cm2

question_text: The sum of the length, breadth and height of a cuboid is 6√3cm and the length of its diagonal is 2√3cm. The total surface area of the cuboid is
answer_text: 96 cm2
answer_explanation: (l+b+h)²=l²+b²+h²+2(lb+bh+hl). Thus 108=12+2(lb+bh+hl), so total surface area=2(lb+bh+hl)=96 cm².

question_text: If the difference of Mode and Median of a data is 24, then the difference of median and mean is
answer_explanation: Mode=3Median-2Mean. Hence Mode-Median=2(Median-Mean)=24, so Median-Mean=12.

question_text: Statement A (Assertion): If product of two numbers is 5780 and their HCF is 17, then their LCM is 340. Statement R (Reason): HCF is always a factor of LCM.
options: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.
answer_text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A)
answer_explanation: 5780 / 17 = 340, so the Assertion is true. The Reason (HCF always divides LCM) is also a true general fact, but it is not what explains why the LCM here equals 340 — that follows from product = HCF × LCM, a different relationship.

question_text: Statement A (Assertion): If the co-ordinates of the mid-points of the sides AB and AC of ∆ABC are D(3,5) and E(-3,-3) respectively, then BC = 20 units Statement R( Reason) : The line joining the mid points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equal to half of it.
options: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is not the correct explanation of assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but reason(R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but reason(R) is true.
answer_text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A)
answer_explanation: D(3,5), E(-3,-3); DE=√[(6)²+(8)²]=10. By midpoint theorem BC=2DE=20. Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A.

question_text: If 49x+51y= 499, 51 x+49 y= 501, then find the value of x and y
answer_text: Adding equations gives 100x+100y=1000, so x+y=10. Subtracting the first from the second gives 2x-2y=2, so x-y=1. Hence x=11/2 and y=9/2.
answer_explanation: Use addition and subtraction to solve the pair.

question_text: In the given figure, O is the centre of circle. Find ∠AQB, given that PA and PB are tangents to the circle and ∠APB= 75°.
answer_text: OA⊥PA and OB⊥PB, so ∠AOB=360°-(90°+90°+75°)=105°. The angle subtended by chord AB at the circle, ∠AQB, is half the central angle, so ∠AQB=52.5°.
answer_explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same chord.

question_text: The length of the minute hand of a clock is 6cm. Find the area swept by it when it moves from 7:05 p.m. to 7:40 p.m. OR In the given figure, arcs have been drawn of radius 7cm each with vertices A, B, C and D of quadrilateral ABCD as centres. Find the area of the shaded region.
answer_text: From 7:05 to 7:40, the minute hand turns 35×6°=210°. Area swept=(210/360)π(6)²=21π=66 cm².
answer_explanation: The minute hand sweeps 6° per minute.

question_text: If sin(A+B) =1 and cos(A-B)= √3/2, 0°< A+B ≤ 90° and A> B, then find the measures of angles A and B. OR Find an acute angle θ when cosθ − sin θ cosθ+sin θ = 1−√3 1+√3 SECTION C Section C consists of 6 questions of 3 marks each. S.No Marks
answer_text: sin(A+B)=1 gives A+B=90°. cos(A-B)=√3/2 and A>B give A-B=30°. Hence A=60°, B=30°.
answer_explanation: Use standard angle values and solve the simultaneous equations.

question_text: Given that √3 is irrational, prove that 5 + 2√3 is irrational.
answer_text: Assume 5+2√3 is rational, say r. Then √3=(r-5)/2 would be rational, contradicting the given fact that √3 is irrational. Hence 5+2√3 is irrational.
answer_explanation: A rational combination would incorrectly make √3 rational.

question_text: If the zeroes of the polynomial x2 +px +q are double in value to the zeroes of the polynomial 2x2 -5x -3, then find the values of p and q.
answer_text: Zeroes of 2x²-5x-3 are 3 and -1/2. Doubled zeroes are 6 and -1. Thus x²+px+q=(x-6)(x+1)=x²-5x-6, so p=-5, q=-6.
answer_explanation: Form the monic polynomial from the transformed roots.

question_text: A train covered a certain distance at a uniform speed. If the train would have been 6 km/h faster, it would have taken 4 hours less than the scheduled time. And, if the train were slower by 6 km/hr ; it would have taken 6 hours more than the scheduled time. Find the length of the journey. OR Anuj had some chocolates, and he divided them into two lots A and B. He sold the first lot at the rate of ₹2 for 3 chocolates and the second lot at the rate of ₹1 per chocolate, and got a total of ₹400. If he had sold the first lot at the rate of ₹1 per chocolate, and the second lot at the rate of ₹4 for 5 chocolates, his total collection would have been ₹460. Find the total number of chocolates he had.
answer_text: Let speed=v and time=t. vt=(v+6)(t-4) and vt=(v-6)(t+6). These give 2v-3t=12 and v-t=6, so t=6 h, v=12 km/h. Distance=72 km.
answer_explanation: Translate the changed-speed conditions into equations.

question_text: Prove the following that- tan3θ + cot3θ = secθ cosecθ – 2 sinθ cosθ 1+ tan2θ 1+ cot2θ
answer_text: LHS=tan³θ/(1+tan²θ)+cot³θ/(1+cot²θ)=tan³θ·cos²θ+cot³θ·sin²θ=sin³θ/cosθ+cos³θ/sinθ=[sin⁴θ+cos⁴θ]/(sinθcosθ). Since sin⁴+cos⁴=1-2sin²cos², LHS=secθcosecθ-2sinθcosθ.
answer_explanation: Rewrite denominators using sec²θ and cosec²θ.

question_text: Prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus OR In the figure XY and X'Y' are two parallel tangents to a circle with centre O and another tangent AB with point of contact C interesting XY at A and X'Y' at B, what is the measure of ∠AOB.
answer_text: Let ABCD be a parallelogram circumscribing a circle. For any tangential quadrilateral, AB+CD=BC+AD. Since AB=CD and BC=AD, 2AB=2BC, so AB=BC. Hence all four sides are equal and the parallelogram is a rhombus.
answer_explanation: Combine the tangent-length property with opposite sides of a parallelogram.

question_text: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting (i) At least one head? (ii) At most one tail? (iii) A head and a tail? SECTION D Section D consists of 4 questions of 5 marks each. S.No Marks
answer_text: Sample space={HH,HT,TH,TT}. (i) At least one head: 3/4. (ii) At most one tail: HH,HT,TH → 3/4. (iii) One head and one tail: HT,TH → 1/2.
answer_explanation: Count equally likely outcomes.

question_text: To fill a swimming pool two pipes are used. If the pipe of larger diameter used for 4 hours and the pipe of smaller diameter for 9 hours, only half of the pool can be filled. Find, how long it would take for each pipe to fill the pool separately, if the pipe of smaller diameter takes 10 hours more than the pipe of larger diameter to fill the pool? OR In a flight of 600km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip was reduced by 200 km/hr from its usual speed and the time of the flight increased by 30 min. Find the scheduled duration of the flight.
answer_text: Let the larger pipe fill in x h and the smaller in x+10 h. Then 4/x+9/(x+10)=1/2. Solving gives x²-16x-80=0, so x=20. Therefore larger pipe:20 h; smaller pipe:30 h.
answer_explanation: Add the fractions of the pool filled by each pipe.

question_text: Prove that if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides in distinct points, then the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. Using the above theorem prove that a line through the point of intersection of the diagonals and parallel to the base of the trapezium divides the non parallel sides in the same ratio.
answer_text: BPT proof: In ΔABC, let DE∥BC. Triangles BDE and CDE have equal areas. Also ar(ADE)/ar(BDE)=AD/DB and ar(ADE)/ar(CDE)=AE/EC; hence AD/DB=AE/EC. For trapezium ABCD with AB∥CD, diagonals intersect at O and a line through O parallel to bases meets AD,BC at P,Q. Apply BPT in the relevant triangles to obtain AP/PD=BQ/QC.
answer_explanation: Repeated application of the Basic Proportionality Theorem gives equal division ratios.

question_text: Due to heavy floods in a state, thousands were rendered homeless. 50 schools collectively decided to provide place and the canvas for 1500 tents and share the whole expenditure equally. The lower part of each tent is cylindrical with base radius 2.8 m and height 3.5 m and the upper part is conical with the same base radius, but of height 2.1 m. If the canvas used to make the tents costs ₹120 per m2, find the amount shared by each school to set up the tents. OR There are two identical solid cubical boxes of side 7cm. From the top face of the first cube a hemisphere of diameter equal to the side of the cube is scooped out. This hemisphere is inverted and placed on the top of the second cube’s surface to form a dome. Find (i) the ratio of the total surface area of the two new solids formed (ii) volume of each new solid formed.
answer_text: For each tent, r=2.8 m, cylinder height=3.5 m, cone height=2.1 m, slant height=3.5 m. Canvas area=2πrh+πrl=2π(2.8)(3.5)+π(2.8)(3.5)=29.4π=92.4 m². For 1500 tents, area=138600 m²; cost=₹16,632,000; share per school=₹332,640.
answer_explanation: Only curved surfaces are covered; multiply by the number of tents and divide equally.

question_text: The median of the following data is 525. Find the values of x and y, if the total frequency is 100 Class interval Frequency 0−100 2 100−200 5 200−300 x 300−400 12 400−500 17 500−600 20 600−700 y 700−800 9 800−900 7 900−1000 4 SECTION E Case study based questions are compulsory.
answer_text: Total frequency: x+y=24. Median class is 500–600. Using 525=500+[(50-(36+x))/20]×100 gives x=9. Hence y=15.
answer_explanation: Use the grouped-data median formula and the total-frequency condition.

question_text: The school auditorium was to be constructed to accommodate at least 1500 people. The chairs are to be placed in concentric circular arrangement in such a way that each succeeding circular row has 10 seats more than the previous one. (i) If the first circular row has 30 seats, how many seats will be there in the 10th row? (ii) For 1500 seats in the auditorium, how many rows need to be there? OR If 1500 seats are to be arranged in the auditorium, how many seats are still left to be put after 10th row? (iii) If there were 17 rows in the auditorium, how many seats will be there in the middle row?
answer_text: (i) a10=30+9×10=120. (ii) Sn=n/2[60+10(n-1)]=5n(n+5)=1500 gives n=15 rows. OR S10=750, so 750 seats remain. (iii) With 17 rows, middle row is 9th: a9=30+8×10=110.
answer_explanation: The seats form an arithmetic progression.

question_text: We all have seen the airplanes flying in the sky but might have not thought of how they actually reach the correct destination. Air Traffic Control (ATC) is a service provided by ground-based air traffic controllers who direct aircraft on the ground and through a given section of controlled airspace, and can provide advisory services to aircraft in non-controlled airspace. Actually, all this air traffic is managed and regulated by using various concepts based on coordinate geometry and trigonometry. At a given instance, ATC finds that the angle of elevation of an airplane from a point on the ground is 60°. After a flight of 30 seconds, it is observed that the angle of elevation changes to 30°. The height of the plane remains constantly as 3000√3 m. Use the above information to answer the questions that follow- (i) Draw a neat labelled figure to show the above situation diagrammatically. (ii) What is the distance travelled by the plane in 30 seconds? OR Keeping the height constant, during the above flight, it was observed that after 15(√3 -1) seconds, the angle of elevation changed to 45°. How much is the distance travelled in that duration. (iii) What is the speed of the plane in km/hr.
answer_text: (i) Draw two observation points on a horizontal line with the plane at constant height 3000√3 m; angles are 60° and 30°. (ii) Initial horizontal distance=3000 m; later distance=9000 m; distance travelled=6000 m. (iii) Speed=6000/30=200 m/s=720 km/h.
answer_explanation: Use tanθ=height/base and convert m/s to km/h.
